newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to keep up flow of 30-year bonds-Bonn's Stark.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to keep up flow of 30-year bonds-Bonn's Stark.

text.p: Bonn plans to keep up the flow of 30-year paper to the market to make sure that this segment is sufficiently supplied with liquidity, state secretary to the German finance ministry Juergen Stark said on Tuesday.
Stark said at a briefing at the finance ministry in answer to a question: "We have made clear that we want to be in this segment and we will be present in it."
Germany launched its first 30-year Bund with great ceremony in 1994, combining the release with the issue of a long-term Bund contract on the DTB futures and options exchange.
But a lack of follow-up issues in this segment of the market forced the withdrawal of the contract.

Stark added however that although the government had the stated aim of making sure that the full length of the maturity curve was adequately supplied with paper, Germany was also aiming to limit its total new debt issuance and could not simply make issues to ensure the market had an even supply.
"We cannot keep raising our new debt issuance," he said. "There is a limit on that, but we want to be present in all areas of the market."

As one means to ensure maximum liquidity in the market, the government was currently considering a proposal by the Bundesbank that all government issues should be grouped directly as federal government issues, he said.
Some government agencies currently issue debt independently of the federal government's own issues.
"If all such agencies were combined under one address, the federal government, then it would increase the volume available," he said.
Shortage of paper in particular sectors has in the past led to deliverability problems for contracts which have German federal issues as their underlying instrument.
